images.caption: View of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. The vicinity of Cape Columbine is depicted, with associated beaches, bays and other water features. The inland area is mainly flat, but low hills including Karringberg (176 m) and Massenberg (160 m) fringe Saldanha Bay. Flanking the bay entrance are also the prominent landmarks of Malgaskop (112 m) and Postberg (193 m).

images.caption: View of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. It shows Saldanha Bay and Langebaan Lagoon, Cape Columbine, the lower reaches of the Berg River, down to its estuary at St Helena Bay, and on its right bank, the stark outlines of the Piketberg. The latter consists of Malmesbury Group shales with granite intrusions, capped by Table Mountain sandstone.
images.alt: View of the West Coast region of the Western Cape, South Africa, taken during ISS Expedition 6. It shows Saldanha Bay and Langebaan Lagoon, Cape Columbine, the lower reaches of the Berg River, down to its estuary at St Helena Bay, and on its right bank, the stark outlines of the Piketberg. The latter consists of Malmesbury Group shales with granite intrusions, capped by Table Mountain sandstone.

images.filename: The coastal region of South Africa (iss071e580719), Swartland.jpg
images.caption: iss071e580719 (Aug. 30, 2024) — The coastal plain of the Western Cape, South Africa, in the winter of 2024. It was pictured from the International Space Station as it orbited 265 miles above. At center is the wheat producing region of the Swartland, with mountains of the Cape Fold Belt forming a backdrop. The greater part of the Swartland is in the catchment of the Berg River which empties into St Helena Bay at bottom left, though the southern part is drained by the Diep River which empties into Table Bay, just out of view to the right. Sediment plumes of these rivers are swept northwards by the cold and nutrient-rich Benguela Current. Cape Columbine, named for one of many local shipwrecks, is near the southern boundary of the image. Its vicinity is protected in a nature reserve, while the vicinity of Langebaan Lagoon is included in the West Coast National Park.
images.alt: iss071e580719 (Aug. 30, 2024) — The coastal plain of the Western Cape, South Africa, in the winter of 2024.
